articles.authors: Qifan Zhang, Wangke Yu, Jingyu Liu, Zhongquan Nie, Yijie Shen, Shirong Lin
institutions: Great Bay Institute for Advanced Study
articles.summary: Structured light fields, featuring unique topological properties and high tunability, have opened new frontiers in light–matter interactions with magnetic systems, yet ultrafast, reconfigurable optical writing of diverse topological magnetic textures remains a significant challenge. Here, we systematically investigate the encoding mechanism of topological light in magnets via the higher-order Poincaré sphere. By relating the light’s winding number to the topological charge of magnetic textures, we establish a light–magnetism topological connection. This framework enables ultrafast, all-optical encoding of diverse topological spin textures─skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and skyrmion bags. …

articles.title: Fourier pixels: unifying bidirectional vectorial light-field generation and sensing at the microscale
articles.authors: Haofan Huang, Zechen Wei, Puxiang Lai
articles.summary: This commentary highlights Fourier pixels, a recent advance in planar optics that enables continuous momentum space engineering and full vectorial light-field manipulation. By replacing discrete resonators with continuous surface topographies, Fourier pixels overcome the near-field coupling and phase discretization limits of classical metasurfaces, providing an alternative route to monolithic on-chip optical processing. They unify light generation and sensing in a single micrometer-scale pixel, enabling simultaneous, bidirectional control of amplitude, phase, and polarization. We discuss the principles, demonstrations, and challenges toward practical on-chip photonic technologies.
